question.text: RBI has mandated that for floating-rate home loans extended to individual borrowers by banks:

answer.text: There shall be no prepayment charges
Prepayment charges of 2% must be levied
Prepayment is not allowed in the first 3 years
Prepayment charges are decided by each bank independently

explanation.text: The Logic: RBI has mandated that there shall be no pre-payment charges on floating-rate home loans extended by banks to individual borrowers. This encourages borrowers to prepay when they have surplus funds and reduces their overall interest burden. The Trap: Prepayment may still be allowed for fixed-rate loans or loans from other lenders, but those may carry charges; the no-charge mandate applies in the floating-rate banking context described. Note: The borrower should always confirm the specific terms of the loan agreement, since the regulatory position can differ for fixed-rate or non-bank loans.
